name: EXP-CLEAN-001 Delete the dead code and the legacy migration, and make the deletion stick
goal:
EXP-CLEAN-001 — Delete the dead code and the legacy migration, and make the deletion stick

OPERATOR REQUEST (2026-10-13, verbatim in substance): there are large blocks of code not being used
at all — dead code, dead imports — and the operator wants all of it gone, along with "this migrations
thing": a legacy migration one of the agents created when the project's structure changed, which the
operator has asked to have removed several times. Each request was verbal and each time the code was
still there afterwards.

WHY IT KEEPS COMING BACK — and therefore what this expedition must actually deliver
A removal that is only performed is a removal that can be undone by the next agent that finds the
code, cannot find a decision explaining why it should not exist, and concludes it is load-bearing.
Nothing in the repository currently records that `synth migrate` was asked to be deleted: there is no
ADR, no CHANGELOG entry, no guard test, and the compiler is not configured to notice dead code at all
(`noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` are both absent from tsconfig.json, so the build is green
with 212 dead declarations in it). So deletion is HALF the work. The other half is three artifacts
that make re-introduction fail loudly: the two tsconfig flags, an ADR stating the decision and its
reason, and a chained removal-manifest test asserting the specific paths and names stay gone.

SEQUENCING (operator decision): this runs AFTER the testing work is addressed. Hard dependencies:
EXP-TEST-001 (e9a83ffda86ca767), EXP-TEST-002 (f6420030064a6f70), EXP-TEST-003 (328c0147b49d2743),
EXP-TEST-004 (a33ac4392da04d0e), EXP-TEST-005 (74c33996d5e7cf32), and EXP-CLI-003 (e47a186cb472a20a).
Rationale: EXP-CLI-003 restructures src/cli into a verb -> loader registry and repoints the test
harness; deleting modules underneath it would guarantee conflicts and would make its load-budget
measurements meaningless. EXP-TEST-005 decides which test files have owners, which determines whether
a "referenced only by tests" module is alive or orphaned — that verdict is an input here, not
something to guess at.

MEASURED INVENTORY (2026-10-13, branch arena/15e0fc51-synth at 21d3aba7, dist rebuilt from source;
every number below was measured, and each is labelled with how strong its evidence is)

D1. THE LEGACY MIGRATION — the operator's specific ask. 519 lines of source:
      src/cli/migrate.ts        260 lines   the `synth migrate` verb: detect, plan, archive, import
      src/migration/detect.ts   140 lines   detectLegacyState
      src/migration/plan.ts      80 lines   buildMigrationPlan, resolveLegacyEventLogPath
      src/migration/types.ts     39 lines
    Plus 12 references inside src/cli/synth.ts, and `migrate` is one of the 33 verbs in the canonical
    COMMANDS list in src/cli/usage.ts — so removing it is a public verb-surface change, not an
    internal cleanup. Evidence it is unused in practice: the 1572-invocation census of a full test run
    records exactly 4 `migrate` calls, and its only test (tests/migration.test.js) is a RED ORPHAN —
    not one of the 115 chain segments, and it currently fails with ENOENT on a temp archive directory
    (verified identical on both the pre- and post-Phase-0 builds, so it is pre-existing). Those 4 calls
    are that broken test. Nothing else in the repository invokes the verb.
    Also in scope, because it is the same confusion in a second place:
      docs/expeditions/EXP-MIGRATE-001.md, docs/governance/convergence-review-migrate-001.md,
      docs/guides/agents/migration-strategy.md,
      docs/guides/agents/migrating-runtime-data-to-synth.md,
      docs/reference/term-migration-report.md, docs/reference/terminology-migration-report.md
        — 1046 lines across 6 files
      examples/legacy-node/ (README.md, package.json, scripts/run.js) — 65 lines
    A DIFFERENT migration that must NOT be confused with the above:
      scripts/generate-npm-task-migration.js (128 lines) + tests/task-npm-migration.test.js (58 lines)
      generated the npm-script -> data/tasks migration. Its OUTPUT is load-bearing: 169 files in
      data/tasks/, including test:all.task.json, which is the canonical 115-segment chain that
      `npm run test:all`, `synth task run` and CI all execute. Neither the generator nor its test is
      chained, and no npm script references the generator, so the generator itself is now dead weight
      — but deleting it must not touch data/tasks/**, and `test:task-npm-adapter` (which IS chained) is
      a different thing again and stays.

D2. COMPILER-VERIFIED DEAD DECLARATIONS — the strongest evidence class, because tsc itself reports
    them. Running `tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters -p tsconfig.json` on the current
    tree: **212 errors across 100 distinct src files**, while the normal build reports 0 errors only
    because both flags are absent from tsconfig.json.
      181 x TS6133  'x' is declared but its value is never read   (dead locals and dead imports)
       26 x TS6196  type declared but never used
        3 x TS6138  property declared but never read
        2 x TS6192  all imports in this line are unused
    Worst files: src/cli/synth.ts 17, src/cli/first-contact.ts 12, src/runtime/replay.ts 8,
    src/domain/execution.ts 8, src/cli/task.ts 7, src/adapters/repository/git.ts 5,
    src/signing/signer.ts 4, src/mission-studio/engine.ts 4.
    Note the interaction with EXP-CLI-003: 17 of the 212 are in synth.ts, which that expedition is
    decomposing. Fix these AFTER it lands, or the counts will have moved.

D3. MODULES UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SHIPPED ENTRY POINT — graph evidence, needs per-candidate proof.
    Transitive closure over static AND dynamic relative imports from the three entry points in
    package.json (bin.synth = dist/cli/entry.js, bin.synth-mcp = dist/distribution/mcp-server.js,
    main = dist/main.js): 304 of 348 dist modules are reachable, **44 are not — 2855 lines of
    compiled JS**, clustered (compiled lines): first-contact 881, environment 722 + providers 152,
    execution 421, cli 299, discovery 84, core 44, mutation 19, capabilities 16, documentation 16,
    types 13, planning 12. Largest: environment/rules.js 333, first-contact/experiment.js 316,
    cli/adapter.js 299, execution/runtime.js 287, environment/orchestrator.js 245,
    first-contact/patterns.js 239, first-contact/scenarios.js 197.
    These are CANDIDATES, not verdicts. Unreachable-from-bin does not equal dead: a module can be
    loaded through a computed specifier, imported directly by a test, be an entry point for a
    distribution artifact not listed in bin, or be reachable only from dist/cli/synth.js — which the
    test harness spawns for 1536 of 1572 invocations even though it is not the shipped bin.
    (dist/cli/synth.js must be added as a fourth root before any deletion decision; EXP-CLI-003
    decides whether it stays a compatibility entry.) An earlier attempt at this measurement in this
    session produced a false answer twice — once by counting a mention in docs/*.md as a reference,
    and once by matching module stems, so that "adapter" appeared to be referenced by 23 test files
    and 230 docs when the match was really adapter-catalog, adapter-registry, etc. Any tool used here
    must resolve real specifiers to real paths and must be spot-checked against a module known to be
    alive and a module known to be dead.

D4. EXPORTED SYMBOLS NEVER REFERENCED — heuristic, weakest evidence class, verify per symbol.
    401 exported functions/consts/classes/types/interfaces/enums in src/**/*.ts whose name appears in
    no other src file, no test and no script. Top files: src/discovery/types.ts 21,
    src/ledger/delivery.ts 17, src/cli/certification-runner.ts 11, src/mission-studio/types.ts 10,
    src/environment/rules.ts 9, src/ledger/writer.ts 9, src/compiler/type-checker.ts 8,
    src/governance/project-mission.ts 8. Known false-positive mechanisms: barrel re-exports
    (`export * from`), symbols reached as `sdk.foo` through a namespace import, and public API surface
    that is intentionally exported for consumers of the package rather than for this repository. A
    symbol that is only re-exported and never called is still dead, but proving that means following
    the barrel chain, not grepping a name.

D5. PUBLIC VERBS THE SUITE NEVER INVOKES — an operator decision, not a silent deletion.
    Of the 33 verbs in COMMANDS, 31 are invoked by the 1572-call census. Two are invoked zero times:
      approval  (src/cli/approval.ts, 155 lines, 3 references in synth.ts)
      intent    (no src/cli/intent.ts; handled inline in synth.ts, 3 references)
    Zero invocations is evidence about the test suite, not about users. Removing a public verb is a
    breaking change; the operator must decide each one explicitly, and `migrate` (D1) is the one case
    where the decision has already been made and repeated.

DELIVERABLES
  1. Remove the legacy migration (D1): the verb, src/migration/**, its 12 references in synth.ts, its
     entry in COMMANDS, tests/migration.test.js, the 6 docs (1046 lines) and examples/legacy-node.
     Decide the generator half of D1 separately and, if it goes, prove data/tasks/** and the
     115-segment chain are untouched by re-running `npm run test:all` before and after.
  2. Fix all 212 compiler-reported dead declarations (D2) and turn `noUnusedLocals` and
     `noUnusedParameters` ON in tsconfig.json permanently. This is the guard that makes dead imports
     fail the build instead of accumulating silently again.
  3. Resolve the 44 unreachable-module candidates (D3) to verdicts — delete, keep-with-reason, or
     keep-because-reachable-from-synth.js — using a resolver that survives the spot-check described
     above, and delete the ones proven dead.
  4. Resolve the 401 unused-export candidates (D4) the same way, following barrel chains.
  5. Put D5 to the operator as an explicit keep/remove decision per verb.
  6. Write ADR-057 (docs/adr/, next free number after ADR-056) recording WHAT was removed, WHY, WHO
     decided, and that re-introducing it requires reversing the ADR — plus a CHANGELOG.md entry for
     the removed public verb. This is the artifact whose absence caused the recurrence.
  7. Add a chained removal-manifest test asserting the deletions hold: no src/migration/**, no
     src/cli/migrate.ts, no `migrate` name in src/cli/usage.ts COMMANDS, no `synth migrate` in the
     help payload, no tests/migration.test.js, no docs/guides/agents/migration-strategy.md, no
     examples/legacy-node/**, and (if removed) no scripts/generate-npm-task-migration.js — while
     data/tasks/** and the chain length remain intact. Register it as a task and append it to
     test:all.task.json so it runs on every chain execution.

ACCEPTANCE
  * `tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters -p tsconfig.json` exits 0, and both flags are
    present in tsconfig.json.
  * `synth migrate` no longer exists: the verb is absent from COMMANDS, `synth help` does not list it,
    and invoking it produces the standard unknown-command envelope. `synth --help` still lists every
    remaining verb and both entry points stay byte-identical across the nine-invocation surface that
    tests/loader-entrypoint.test.js guards.
  * The removal-manifest test is a chain segment and passes; deliberately re-adding one removed path
    makes it fail (proved, then reverted).
  * `npm run test:all` stays green and its segment count is the pre-change count plus the new
    manifest test, minus any removed migration test task. No currently-green orphan turns red. The
    four known pre-existing red orphans (synth-cli-repo, migration, first-contact-cli,
    governance-report-cli) are accounted for explicitly — note that removing tests/migration.test.js
    retires one of them rather than fixing it, and the evidence must say so instead of letting the
    red count silently drop.
  * `synth verify` ok; `synth doctor` 12/12; `synth log`/`checkpoint` still report real counts and
    layouts (at the time of writing: 473 events, segmented layout).
  * Every deletion in the evidence is labelled with its evidence class — compiler-verified,
    graph-reachable, census-backed, or heuristic — and every heuristic deletion names the check that
    confirmed it. Line counts removed are reported per category, with the source line total and the
    compiled-JS total given separately.
  * dist-manifest, determinism and proof re-baselined deliberately, with the new file count and
    rootHash stated (at the time of writing: 1050 files, rootHash 3a59324b...).

NON-GOALS
  * Not the test inventory or file-ownership guard (EXP-TEST-005), not suite merging (EXP-TEST-002),
    not the sharded runner (EXP-TEST-003), not the logging/failure envelope (EXP-TEST-001), not
    explicit-environment fields (EXP-TEST-004). Where a module is alive only because an orphaned test
    imports it, the verdict waits for EXP-TEST-005 rather than pre-empting it.
  * Not the CLI decomposition, the load budgets or the dispatcher graph (EXP-CLI-003). This
    expedition deletes what is left after that restructuring, not instead of it.
  * No output-contract changes beyond the removal of the `migrate` verb. The four operator decisions
    settled in EXP-CLI-001 (JSON envelope for --version with --human for the bare string; no status
    INFO line on stderr; TTY-aware help; one unified verb list) stay exactly as they are.
  * Not the four source-path guard tests (tests/verify-engine, tests/artifact-policy,
    tests/governance-orchestration, tests/impact-analyzer), which reference src/cli/synth.ts by path
    and must never be deleted.
  * Not deleting data/tasks/** or anything the 115-segment chain executes.

AMENDMENT to the EXP-CLEAN-001 inventory (operator instruction 2026-10-14: add the artifact-policy
leak, commit the measurement tooling so the numbers are reproducible by anyone, and "make it right"
on the tsconfig flags inside this expedition). Four additions and two corrections. Nothing above is
rewritten; the original measured goal stands as written.

D6. ARTIFACT-POLICY LEAK — test byproducts are written into a tracked, committable directory, and a
    ceremony commit then sweeps them into history. Three parts, all measured:
      (a) src/cli/certification-runner.ts:423 writes `certification-report-${Date.now()}.json` into
          options.outputDir, and tests/certification-framework.test.js:44 ASSERTS that a report file
          was written ("explain mode must write a report file"). That test is chained, so every full
          `npm run test:all` leaves three new untracked timestamped files under
          proof/certifications/. Observed twice in two consecutive sessions (1791937544354/5/6 and
          1791969422089/8/9), cleaned both times.
      (b) Commit 5907889 ("EXPEDITION_REFINED expedition 2c13ca22") committed three of them —
          526 lines each, 1578 lines of byproduct — alongside 3 ledger files. Mechanism:
          src/ledger/ceremony.ts:339-366 builds `existing` from the pathspecs its CALLER passes and
          commits with `git commit -m <msg> -- ...existing`. That caller's list included
          proof/certifications/, which is NOT in AUTO_COMMIT_INCLUDE_ROOTS
          (src/state/artifact-policy.ts:105 = [".synth/data", "proof/expeditions", "AGENTS.md"]).
          So there are two competing definitions of ceremony-commit scope and the broader one won.
      (c) scripts/check-artifact-policy.js PASSES over this (2195 tracked paths, "rules durable:13
          input:1 derived:1 cache:4 legacy:2"), because the reports classify as committable. No
          existing guard catches either half of this.
    Deliverable: make certification reports write to a temp dir (or classify proof/certifications as
    derived and ignore it), collapse ceremony-commit scope to ONE authority, and decide whether the
    1578 lines already in history under proof/certifications/ come back out. This is the same
    invariant class as "reads never write" and "derived state never blocks work" from the
    artifact-policy expedition; it is a leak of exactly what those invariants forbid.

D7. THE MEASUREMENT TOOLING IS NOW COMMITTED (774a322), so every number in this goal is
    reproducible by anyone rather than only by the session that measured it. The four throwaway
    scripts in /tmp did not survive a sandbox reset.
      npm run audit:module-graph       eager graph per entry point + unreachable modules, reported
                                       BOTH from the shipped roots (bin + main) and with
                                       dist/cli/synth.js added as a harness root
      npm run audit:unused-exports     exported names no other src file, test or script mentions,
                                       each labelled barrel-exposed or not
      npm run audit:dead-declarations  tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters, reported
                                       by diagnostic code and worst file; --max N turns it into a gate
      npm run measure:cli-startup      median-of-N wall timings with a mandatory untouched control;
                                       --compare A.json B.json prints control-adjusted deltas
    All four are registered as tasks in data/tasks/ and routed through scripts/task-adapter-shim.js,
    because tests/task-npm-adapter.test.js (chained, segment ~95) requires every npm script to
    delegate to the task engine — adding them as direct node invocations turned the chain red.
    They report rather than gate and are deliberately NOT chained: a gate that fails on the day it is
    added teaches people to ignore gates. Known side effect: four unchained tasks take
    `synth task doctor`'s orphaned-entry-point count from 151 to 155, the same warning class as the
    115 unreachable orphan test files that EXP-TEST-005 owns.
    Two self-checks are built in, because the original measurement was wrong twice before it was
    right: audit-module-graph refuses to report when fewer than half of dist/ is reachable (the
    signature of a resolver bug — one such bug reported 3 of 348 reachable and looked like a
    catastrophic finding rather than an absolute-vs-relative path-key mismatch), and
    audit-unused-exports fails if three known-used symbols appear as candidates (an earlier version
    counted a docs/*.md mention as a reference and reported zero dead modules — wrong in the
    comfortable direction, which would have hidden the finding entirely).

D8. THE TSCONFIG FLAGS ARE A NAMED ACCEPTANCE GATE, NOT A SUB-ITEM (operator: "let's change that,
    make it right in the expedition we created for it"). The finished state is all three of:
      1. all 212 compiler-reported dead declarations removed (181 TS6133, 26 TS6196, 3 TS6138,
         2 TS6192, across 100 files);
      2. `noUnusedLocals: true` and `noUnusedParameters: true` present in tsconfig.json permanently,
         so `npm run build` itself refuses to be green with dead code in it;
      3. `audit:dead-declarations --max 0` chained into test:all as the guard against either the
         count growing again or the flags being removed — at which point the flags make the script
         redundant for src/ and it survives only as a guard on the flags.
    A ratchet is available IMMEDIATELY and does not need this expedition: chaining
    `audit:dead-declarations --max 212` today fails only if the count GROWS. Sequencing constraint
    that must be respected: 17 of the 212 are in src/cli/synth.ts, which EXP-CLI-003 is decomposing,
    so fixing them before that lands means fixing them twice. Order is CLI-003, then this.

D9. TWO MEASURED CORRECTIONS to numbers in the goal above.
      * The unreachable set is 44 modules / 2855 compiled lines under BOTH root sets — adding
        dist/cli/synth.js as a fourth root reaches nothing the shipped entry points do not
        (304 reachable either way). The goal assumed that adding it might shrink the candidate list;
        measured with the committed resolver, it does not. The caveat still holds for computed
        specifiers and direct test imports.
      * Unused exports are 402, not 401: the committed resolver also parses `export { a, b as c }`
        lists, which the throwaway version missed. 109 of the 402 are barrel-exposed, i.e. re-
        exported wholesale by some index and therefore possibly public API of the published package.
        Worst files unchanged: discovery/types.ts 21, ledger/delivery.ts 17,
        cli/certification-runner.ts 11, mission-studio/types.ts 10, environment/rules.ts 9.

CORRECTION OF MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM. On 2026-10-13 I reported that the ceremony auto-commit "stages
only durable state paths" and cited AUTO_COMMIT_INCLUDE_ROOTS as the authority, then relied on that
to conclude `git add -N` was safe for untracked source files. The conclusion happened to be right
(the source files were not swept in) but the premise was wrong: the ceremony writer commits the
pathspecs its caller passes, and 5907889 proves that list can include proof/certifications/. Anyone
reasoning about what a ceremony commit will pick up must read the caller, not the constant.

============================================================
D10. SCOPE EXTENSION — FULL CLI VALUE AND COMPLEXITY AUDIT
Operator instruction, 2026-10-14: "extend scope on EXP-CLEAN-001 to do a full CLI audit and analize what is worth keeping, what can be done in a different way and what is totally overengineered."
============================================================
This adds a product/workflow and architecture audit to the existing dead-code cleanup. It is not limited to unreachable modules, unused declarations, or the two zero-invocation verbs in D5. Code can be reachable and thoroughly tested yet still implement needless complexity. Conversely, absence from the test census is not proof that a command has no users or value. Preserve the original goal and prior refinements; this is an additive amendment, not an erasure of earlier decisions.

AUDIT COVERAGE
  1. Inventory the entire actual CLI at execution time: shipped entry point, compatibility entry point, every registered/public top-level verb, every implemented subcommand, aliases, flags and defaults, help/documentation exposure, hidden/legacy routes, and recursive CLI callers. Reconcile the registry, dispatch implementations and help rather than treating any one of them as a complete inventory. Recompute all historical counts after CLI-003 and the testing expeditions; do not treat the old 33-verb census or unused-code counts as current facts.
  2. Follow real operator journeys, not just individual handlers: initialization/onboarding, planning and mission/expedition work, validation and governance, evidence and completion, delivery/seal, recovery, reporting, and adapter/task configuration. Record the necessary steps, required parameters, repeated information already held in state, failure/recovery paths and side effects. Look for unnecessary ceremonies and commands that force an operator to coordinate internal implementation details manually.
  3. Trace implementation ownership for each surface: handler, shared helpers, authoritative state/configuration source, adapters, gates, persistence and Git/network effects. Identify duplicate authorities, redundant checks or abstractions, overlapping commands, excessive indirection, needless bootstrap/loading, inconsistent defaults and configuration that is accepted but not applied. Distinguish intentional safety invariants from accidental ceremony; simpler must not mean bypassing an actual integrity boundary.
  4. Ground usage and compatibility claims in resolved imports/call sites, tasks/CI, tests, documentation, published API contracts and available operator evidence. Label unknown usage as unknown. A docs mention is not an executed call; a test-only caller is not proof of production use; no observed calls is not authorization to remove a public surface.

REQUIRED DECISION REPORT
  Produce a versioned, reproducible inventory and a decision matrix covering every inventoried command/subcommand. For each, record:
    - user problem and value; implementation and consumer evidence;
    - KEEP as-is, SIMPLIFY internally, CONSOLIDATE/REPLACE with an existing mechanism, REMOVE candidate, or INVESTIGATE with a named unresolved question;
    - whether the design is proportionate to its job or overengineered, with specific evidence (not a label based only on file size, line count or personal preference);
    - a simpler alternative where proposed: fewer steps/parameters, an existing verb, a shared internal service, or the proper adapter rather than another public command;
    - tradeoffs, invariants preserved, compatibility and migration implications, tests affected, measurable expected benefit, decision owner and implementation owner.
  Compare the current and proposed end-to-end workflows. Include before/after examples and a prioritized simplification plan. Explicitly identify redundant verbs and public concepts, and explain what remains necessary even when it is complex. Do not preselect a command-count reduction target or invent new verbs to make the audit appear productive.

ACCEPTANCE AND IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY
  - No public or implemented route silently omitted from the inventory: differences among dispatch, help and docs are recorded and resolved or explicitly assigned.
  - Every keep/remove/simplify judgment is traceable to evidence; heuristic candidates are confirmed before deletion. Unknowns and deferred findings have a reason and an owner rather than disappearing into a summary.
  - Review the proposed target CLI and public keep/remove/rename/merge decisions with the operator BEFORE implementing those interface changes. The existing explicit decision to remove `migrate` stands; this amendment is not blanket approval to remove other commands.
  - Execute confirmed dead-code removal and approved simplifications within CLEAN-001's scope; substantial new behavior or changes already owned elsewhere remain with that owner, rather than expanding cleanup into an unbounded rewrite. Preserve working contracts and safety invariants unless a change is explicitly approved and documented.
  - Carry forward CLI-003's load-budget, entry-point parity, real-count and no-new-test-regression guards. Retain the permanent compiler/removal guards required by D8 and the original goal. Record before/after measurements and evidence; do not claim a speedup from incomparable runs.
  - Produce the full audit and decision report even where the recommendation is to KEEP a component. A list of deleted files alone does not satisfy this scope extension.

SEQUENCING AND EXISTING OWNERSHIP
  Existing hard dependencies and draft status remain unchanged: CLI-003 first, testing work before code cleanup. This amendment does not start or approve CLEAN-001 and does not widen CLI-003 into a general CLI redesign.
  Reconcile overlapping work explicitly: the governance-cluster audit (761c9be33f165253), legacy-verb folding (29b9a3704eb1287c), the src/scripts DRY drafts (e38aa99f7f2593af / 9ab1218c6f872c60), and the older legacy-removal expedition (912a468ae9bf5bd6). Reuse their findings and record ownership boundaries; do not silently cancel them, duplicate their implementation, or assume a historical inventory is current.
  LIFE-002 (f0912d1aeee16213) retains ownership of expedition lifecycle/commit consolidation and adapter-configuration consolidation. This audit may assess the resulting experience and report gaps, but must not build a competing commit authority or another configuration loader.

D6 OWNERSHIP CLARIFICATION — preserve the earlier finding, correct the delivery assignment
  D6(b)'s single ceremony-commit scope authority is implemented by LIFE-002, as already specified in its charter; CLEAN-001 verifies and consumes that result rather than implementing it a second time. CLEAN-001 retains the certification-test byproduct/output-location and artifact-policy guard work in D6(a)/(c).
  The operator's existing decision is to KEEP the 1578 lines of already-committed certification byproducts. The earlier text asking whether to remove those historical reports is therefore resolved: do not delete them as cleanup. Prevent future accidental accumulation instead. No additional dependency is silently added by this clarification; if unfinished LIFE-002 work blocks the relevant acceptance check, record that dependency explicitly before implementation.
